subject: Variable Log2FC and pvalue when running mutliple vs single comparisons

messages.author: 7ddd90c765288ead
messages.subject: Variable Log2FC and pvalue when running mutliple vs single comparisons
parts:
Hi MSstats team,

I noticed that I get pretty different Log2FC and pvalues if I run a single comparison in my contrast file vs multiple comparisons. For example, if I run Non-treated vs Drug A as the only comparison in my contrast file, I obtain ~1290 significant proteins. If I run Non-treated vs Drug A, and Non-treated vs Drug B, it changes the profile of significant proteins in the original comparison (Non-treated vs Drug A) from 1290 significant proteins to ~1800. In some cases, proteins gain significance and in other cases they lose significance. My understanding is that contrasts should be independent of each other, but is this not the case? The data changes pretty dramatically so I am wondering what steps I should take next. Happy to get any feedback or suggestions. 
Many thanks,
Nadia

Hi Mateusz,

Thanks for your reply! I'm using artMS to run MSstats, so I'm using the following files listed below. It is too many to attach, so you can find all these files in the Google Drive folder at the following link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1b5FmxIlCZvJTWSSRNhKYxSdhCExtI0Xa?usp=sharing 

--evidence file: evidence_07052023.txt
--keys file: keys_07052023.txt
--config file for vehicle vs Drug A:  config_contrast_1.yaml
--config file for vehicle vs Drug A and vehicle vs Drug B: config_contrast_2.yaml
--contrast file for vehicle vs Drug A: contrast_1_07052023.txt
--contrast file for vehicle vs Drug A and vehicle vs Drug B: contrast_2_07052023.txt

This is the code that I'm running:
____________________________________________________________________________________
library(data.table)
library(stringr)
library(artMS)
library(yaml)
library(MSstats)

setwd("/Users/narang/Documents/contrast_test/")

artmsQuantification("config_contrast_1.yaml")

artmsQuantification("config_contrast_2.yaml")
____________________________________________________________________________________

Here are my MSstats arguments (you can also find it in my config file):
msstats:
  enabled: 1
  msstats_input: ~
  profilePlots: none
  normalization_method: equalizeMedians
  normalization_reference: ~
  summaryMethod: TMP
  MBimpute: 0.0
  censoredInt: NA
  feature_subset: all
  n_top_feature: 3
  logTrans: 2
  remove_uninformative_feature_outlier: 1
  min_feature_count: 2
  equalFeatureVar: yes
  remove50missing: no
  fix_missing: ~
  maxQuantileforCensored: 0.999
  use_log_file: no
  append: no
  log_file_path: ~
  featureSubset: highQuality
____________________________________________________________________________________

I also put in the folder the output that I'm getting when running the two contrasts:

--vehicle vs Drug A: contrast_1_07052023_results.txt
--vehicle vs Drug A and vehicle vs Drug B: contrast_2_07052023_results.txt

For example, protein Q8WWC4 goes from a Log2FC of -4.909275 to -2.6064827 in the two different runs with nothing changed, except the contrast file. However, my understanding is that contrasts should be independent of each other and this should not be the case, as it strongly changes my output depending on how many contrasts I'm running at any given time. 

Please let me know if I can provide any additional info! 
Best and thanks,
Nadia

messages.subject: Re: Variable Log2FC and pvalue when running mutliple vs single comparisons
parts:
Hi,


while running artMS code I can see a message:

WARNING! the number of unique conditions in evidence file are different from the conditions in contrast!
                                  All the extra conditions will be deleted from the evidence file

I'm not sure what it means exactly and I contacted developers of artMS to check that, but it's most likely what's affecting the output.
I can't run MSstats workflow with your data directly (artMS converts data n a different way, we require evidence, proteinGroups and annotation), but I tested this issue on a different data set and noticed no difference in log-fold changes. My advice is to analyze your data directly with MSstats and use artMS only after we get an explanation for that warning message. Please don't hesitate to contact us in case of any troubles or questions while running MSstats.

Kind regards,
Mateusz
